blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Home Extension Cost in Southbank in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking of extending in Southbank? We break down costs, council fees, and design factors to help you budget.
body: Home extensions in Southbank are a popular way to add space without moving. In 2026, costs typically range from $2,000 to $3,500 per square metre, depending on the complexity of the design and your site's conditions. Henny Pty Ltd has seen everything from single-room additions to full second-storey builds in the Southbank area.

Council approval is a major factor. Southbank falls under the City of Melbourne, which has specific heritage and zoning rules. A standard extension can take 3-6 months to get a permit. Working with a builder like Henny who knows the local process speeds things up and avoids costly delays.

The type of extension matters. A ground-floor addition is cheapest, while a second-storey involves structural work and scaffolding. For a typical 40-square-metre extension in Southbank, you're looking at $80,000 to $140,000. Add a bathroom or kitchen and that figure goes up by 20-30 percent.

Material choices also affect the budget. Brick and glass are common in Southbank for their modern look and durability. The cost of a brick extension is around $2,500 per square metre installed, while glass walls can cost more but add light and value. Henny can advise on the best materials for your build.

Don't forget the extras like landscaping, new flooring, and painting. Many Southbank homeowners budget an extra 10-15% for finishing touches. We recommend getting a fixed-price contract from Henny to avoid surprises — we've done this for dozens of local projects.

Timing is tight in Southbank. Most extensions take 4-6 months from approval to handover. Winter can slow things down due to weather, but Henny plans around this. We've completed extensions in Como and Toorak that came in on schedule, even in wet months.

Financing is another key factor. Many homeowners use equity or savings. There are also government grants for energy-efficient extensions. Henny can help you with feasibility checks before you commit, so you know exactly what's involved.

In summary, a Southbank home extension in 2026 is a solid investment. With Henny's fixed-price approach and local know-how, you can expect a high-quality build without the stress. Contact us for a free on-site quote.

blogPosts.title: Best Time to Pour Concrete in Melbourne Winter
blogPosts.excerpt: Melbourne's winter can be tricky for concrete. Our guide covers the best months, curing tips, and why Southbank builders plan ahead.
body: Pouring concrete in Melbourne winter is a challenge even for experienced builders. The ideal temperature for concrete is 10-25 degrees Celsius, and winter in Southbank often dips below that. Henny Pty Ltd schedules pours between March and May for the best results, when the ground is still warm and frost is rare.

Cold weather slows down curing. If concrete freezes, it can lose up to 50% of its strength. In Southbank, we use blankets and heaters to keep it warm, especially for foundations. Our team has done this on projects across Fitzroy and St Kilda, and it works.

Wind is another factor. The Southbank area near the river gets strong gusts that can dry concrete too fast, causing cracks. We time our pours for calm days and use windbreaks. The Maitland project in Toorak was a winter pour and it held up perfectly.

Summer is the opposite problem — too hot, and the concrete dries too fast. We prefer spring or early autumn for large slabs. For smaller jobs, like paths, winter can work if you're careful. Henny uses additives to slow setting in heat and speed it up in cold.

The cost of concrete in Southbank varies. A standard driveway slab is $80-$120 per square metre. Exposed aggregate costs more but looks great. We always advise getting a fixed-price contract to cover weather-related delays — something we've offered for years.

Finally, plan ahead. Melbourne weather is unpredictable. Henny builds in a 10-day window for concrete pours to account for rain. With our local experience, we can pour year-round if the conditions are right. Ask us for a site assessment.

blogPosts.title: Design and Construct vs Construction Management in Southbank
blogPosts.excerpt: Not sure which building method suits your Southbank project? We compare design and construct with construction management to help you decide.
body: Design and construct (D&C) and construction management are two common approaches in Southbank. With D&C, you have one contract for both design and build. Henny Pty Ltd offers this as a single-point solution, which means less paperwork and no finger-pointing between the architect and builder.

Construction management is different. You hire a builder as a manager to oversee trades, but you contract with each one separately. This gives you more control but also more risk. In Southbank, many homeowners prefer D&C because it's simpler and cheaper when things go wrong.

Cost is a major difference. With D&C, you get a fixed price upfront. With construction management, costs can vary as you change things. Henny has delivered D&C projects in Como and the Maitland that came in on budget, while construction management works best for large, complex jobs.

Time is another factor. D&C is faster because the builder and designer work together from day one. Construction management can be slower if there are disputes. For a typical Southbank renovation, D&C saves 2-3 months.

Quality is similar in both if the right team is involved. Henny uses the same trades for both methods. The main difference is who holds the risk. With D&C, it's with us. With construction management, it's with you. That's why most Southbank clients choose D&C.

Ultimately, D&C is best for most residential projects in Southbank. Henny's fixed-price contracts give you certainty. Construction management is for when you have your own designers and want more hands-on control. Either way, we can help.

blogPosts.title: Southbank Building Trends 2026: What's Popular in New Homes
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the top trends in Southbank building for 2026, from sustainable materials to open-plan living, with insights from Henny.
body: Southbank's building scene in 2026 is all about sustainability and efficiency. Henny Pty Ltd sees more clients asking for solar panels, double-glazed windows, and recycled materials. The cost of these upgrades has come down, making them standard in new builds.

Open-plan living is still king. Kitchens that flow into living areas are essential, with islands for seating. In Southbank, we've installed luxury islands with seating for six. They're a centrepiece for modern family life. The trend is for oversized, functional spaces.

Outdoor living is big too. Decks and courtyards that connect to the indoors are common. In Southbank, we use glass doors to merge the two. The Kerr Street project in Fitzroy did this beautifully, and the results speak for themselves.

Smart homes are on the rise. Automation for lighting, blinds, and security is now standard. Henny integrates these as part of the build, not aftermarket. It's cheaper and ensures it all works together. Many Southbank homes are fully integrated.

Colours are trending toward neutrals. Matte black is popular for hardware and windows, while walls stay white or warm grey. Henny uses this on many projects. It complements the natural light in Southbank's apartments.

Finally, there's a push for ethical building. Clients want to know where materials come from. Henny sources locally where possible, cutting down on transport and supporting Victorian suppliers. It's a win for everyone.
